focus.jnote: The AI scare cooled overnight. US stock futures rose Wednesday as SpaceX's results renewed enthusiasm for the AI trade ahead of earnings from Tesla and Meta; S&P 500 futures gained 0.3% and Nasdaq-100 futures climbed 0.5% after the major averages closed mixed. The tape says earnings beat fear for now, with the VIX back at 17.4 from 18.7 yesterday. That follows a mixed Tuesday: the Dow advanced 1% to 52,494.88, the Nasdaq Composite ended at 26,424.82 (down 0.02%), and the S&P 500 gained 0.3% to 7,712.57. Oil stays the wild card — crude rose to ~$99.58 on October 21, up ~1.8% from the prior day, and is up ~10% over the past month. And rates are heavy: the 10-year held steady near 5.12% as rising oil prices intensified inflation concerns. This is a headline-driven, earnings-heavy tape — exactly where a Sniper trades small and only on confirmed setups.
focus.notdown: LAD is today's clean bullish post-earnings gap. Lithia Motors delivered better-than-expected Q3 results, with adjusted diluted EPS of $10.34 beating the $9.78 estimate by 5.7%. The company reported record quarterly revenue of $9.9 billion, $190 million above forecasts, and raised its quarterly dividend by 7% to $0.75. The scanner boarded it bullish and graded it A+, but be honest about the catch: the reaction came on near-zero relative volume (0.00×, far below the 1.3× bar), the implied move was 9.1% versus a realized gap of 6.5%, and no open-interest data was returned — so this is a half-size, confirm-at-9:35 name, verify liquidity manually, not a table-pounder.
focus.notup: T is today's bearish post-earnings gap — a textbook “sell-the-news” on a beat. AT&T shares fell about 4.6% premarket after Q3 revenue and adjusted earnings beat consensus while postpaid phone subscriber additions came in below expectations. AT&T also raised its full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to ~$2.40 and maintained its free-cash-flow target of at least $18 billion. The scanner boarded it bearish (B+), but the same thin-volume caveat applies — a beat-and-raise gapping DOWN on a subscriber miss is a fragile bearish thesis that can snap back on a dip-buy; half size and validate direction at 9:35.

On top of the gap math: oil near $99 on Hormuz risk, a 10Y at ~5.12% with a likely December hike priced in, and Tesla & Meta reporting after the close mean headline risk is everywhere tonight. The two boarded names are real Type A gaps, but both printed on near-zero relative volume — neither clears the 1.3× confirmation bar, and LAD returned no open-interest data. Half size, A-grade only, confirm 4-VAL at 9:35; if the volume/direction doesn't hold, stand aside. Cash is a position.
